footer.aboutText: This pilot-style quiz is inspired by broad thinking skills associated with aviation, including checklists, focus, navigation sense, weather awareness, instrument logic, fuel planning, and calm decision-making. It is for entertainment and curiosity only, not an official flight school exam, pilot certification test, medical assessment, or aviation qualification.

stageGroups.title: Preflight Basics
stageGroups.encouragement: Good start. Your first pilot score is locked in.

questions.prompt: Before a flight, which habit is most useful?
A checklist says: lights, fuel, route, weather. Which item was skipped: lights, fuel, weather?
A pilot faces east and turns right. Which direction is next?
What should usually happen before a final go/no-go decision?
choices: A calm review of key checks

questions.prompt: Which pair is most useful for staying focused?
If north is at the top of a map, which side is east?
Which item sounds like an instrument check?
A list reads: brakes, lights, fuel, radio. Which item came second?
Which checklist style is safest?
A heading changes from 090 to 180. Which direction did it move toward?

stageGroups.title: Navigation Checks
stageGroups.encouragement: Nice focus. The final round moves into flight decisions.

questions.prompt: Which condition most directly reduces what a pilot can see?
Altitude readings are 1000, 1200, 1400, 1600. What comes next if the pattern continues?
A pilot plans 20 minutes out, 20 minutes back, and 10 minutes for checks. What is the total time?
A route goes north, then east, then south. Which direction would return directly to the start if distances match?
Weather is changing faster than expected. What is the strongest concern?
choices: Conditions may no longer match the plan
The map has too many colors

questions.prompt: Fuel shows 120 minutes. Planned flying is 70 minutes and extra planning adds 25. What remains?
If a checkpoint is 15 minutes away and the next is 20 minutes after that, what is the combined time?
Which reading pattern looks steady?
A direct route is shorter but crosses worse weather. What should be weighed carefully?
Which item belongs most with flight planning numbers?
A route saves 8 minutes but adds uncertain weather. What is the strongest concern?
choices: The weather uncertainty may outweigh the time saving

questions.prompt: In a stressful situation, which order is most sensible?
A plane has 90 minutes of fuel. The route takes 55 minutes and the alternate takes 20 more minutes. How much fuel time remains?
Only verified information should guide the final call. A report is useful but unverified. What comes first?
choices: Verify it or treat it cautiously

questions.prompt: Two issues appear at once: uncertain weather and a minor comfort issue. What comes first?
A fuel estimate seems too optimistic. What is the best response?
choices: Trust it because it feels nice

questions.prompt: A pilot hears two conflicting updates. What is the best next step?
Which choice shows good priority thinking?
A route change looks faster but leaves less margin. What should be checked?
choices: Whether the margin is still acceptable

questions.prompt: Before committing to a final decision, which habit helps most?
